title: Three nominally independent risk controls on the SparkLend Instance are all set to the same 5,000,000 USDS figure
content:
The same number appears three times in different control surfaces. `LIMIT_USDS_MINT` has `maxAmount` 5,000,000 USDS (A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.2.1.1.2.1.1). The SparkLend deposit rate limit has `maxAmount` 5,000,000 USDS (A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.2.4.1). The Instance's off-chain Maximum Exposure is 5,000,000 USDS (A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.2.5.2).

These are genuinely different controls: one bounds creation of USDS at the vault, one bounds the rate at which it can be pushed into a specific venue, one is an off-chain exposure policy for the Instance. Defence in depth normally means each catches a different failure at a different level.

With identical values they collapse into one effective constraint. No control binds before the others, so none provides a warning margin — the mint limit cannot be reached while leaving deposit headroom, and the exposure policy is never breached before an onchain limit stops the transaction.

This is coherent for a launch configuration where the entire Instance is capped at one number and the layers are placed for future divergence. But it means the current posture supplies redundancy — three places to stop the same excess — rather than graduated risk detection. Whether that is a deliberate simplification or an artifact of copying one figure across three documents cannot be determined from the text.

The interesting question the observation raises: which of the three is intended to be the binding one as the Instance scales? The Capital Ratio Requirement of 25% (A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.2.5.3) is the only control expressed as a ratio, so it is the only one that scales with the position rather than being reset by hand.
description: The USDS mint limit, the deposit rate limit and the Maximum Exposure share one value, so the controls bind simultaneously rather than layering.
